Article Title: 97% of serious gamers say gaming helps them connect with like-minded people: Infinix-CMR study
Article Text:
Key findings of the Infinix-CMR study

One of the major findings of the survey is that socialising has emerged as one of the leading motivations for mobile gaming. Nearly half of both gaming audiences cite socialising with friends and others as a reason to play, including 45% of Serious Gamers and 51% of Hyper-Casual/Casual Gamers.

For 97% of Serious Gamers, gaming helps them connect with like-minded people and communities. The sentiment is equally strong among Hyper-Casual/Casual Gamers, with 85% agreeing.

Gaming decisions are heavily shaped by trusted circles. Among Serious Gamers, 88% identify friends, family and gaming communities as major influences on their choice of games. This extends to device consideration as well, with word of mouth (67%) and recommendations from friends and family (66%) emerging as important influences.

Some of the most meaningful gaming moments happen when friends come together after a long day. The study found that 51% of Serious Gamers and 49% of Hyper-Casual/Casual Gamers stay up late to try game updates or play with friends. That connection also creates a sense of missing out. Around 40% of Serious Gamers report feeling left out when they miss gaming conversations, while 54% of casual gamers experience some level of disconnection. Gaming, for many, has become an ongoing social conversation they want to remain part of.

For Gen Z, how they play is increasingly a reflection of who they are. A 92% of Serious Gamers believe they can express their personality better through gaming. Further, 87% of Serious Gamers and 79% of Hyper-Casual/Casual Gamers say their gaming setup represents their identity. This extends into virtual worlds, with 82% of Serious Gamers saying their in-game avatars, skins and outfits reflect their personal style.

While gamers are investing more time and identity into their gaming experiences, device limitations continue to interrupt play. Battery drain affects 62% of Serious Gamers, while 60% of Hyper-Casual/Casual Gamers report overheating as a concern.

As mentioned above, the survey comes ahead of the Infinix GT 50 Pro launch on October 27. The smartphone is teased to come with its "Game Together" ecosystem, bringing together a gaming smartphone, GT NX Controller, GT NX Station, MagCharge Cooler 2.0 and cloud gaming capabilities.

Gaming is becoming more than just a way to pass time for Gen Z, with most young gamers in India saying it helps them connect with like-minded people. According to a new study by Infinix India and CyberMedia Research (CMR), 97% of serious gamers and 85% of casual gamers said gaming helps them build connections and find communities. The study surveyed 2,057 smartphone users aged 16 to 25 across 16 Indian cities. Released ahead of the Infinix GT 50 Pro launch on October 27, the findings highlight how friendships, shared gaming sessions and online communities are shaping young Indians’ gaming habits.The study examined two distinct gaming audiences: Serious Gamers, who spend more than 12 hours gaming weekly, typically in sessions exceeding 120 minutes, and Hyper-Casual/Casual Gamers, who play up to 11 hours a week, generally in sessions of up to an hour.The findings reveal a generation for whom gaming extends well beyond entertainment. Gaming is no longer a boys’ club. Nearly one in three are women, with female participation reaching 36% among hyper-casual gamers, which reflects how gaming has become a mainstream social activity across gender lines.Miraj Gupta, CMO, Infinix India, said, "For years, conversations around gaming smartphones have largely been about performance, frame rates and benchmarks.But gaming today is also about people. It is friends coming together for a quick gaming session after work, couples finding a new way to spend an evening, or siblings waiting to play their favourite game together. The Infinix–CMR study reinforces what we have been observing: Gen Z doesn't just play games, it plays together. With the GT 50 Pro, we're taking that understanding beyond the smartphone and building an ecosystem that makes gaming more connected, flexible and social. Because the future of mobile gaming isn't just about how well you play, but also about who you play with."Prabhu Ram, Vice President - Industry Research Group, CyberMedia Research (CMR), said, "Gaming is increasingly becoming a way for India’s Gen Z to connect, build communities and express its identity. Its influence extends well beyond gameplay, shaping how young consumers discover games, evaluate devices and personalise their experiences. Yet battery drain and overheating remain persistent constraints. For device makers, the opportunity lies in delivering a more complete gaming experience, where sustained performance complements the social and personal dimensions of play. "
Article Summary: 97% of serious gamers and 85% of casual gamers said gaming helps them build connections and find communities. The study surveyed 2,057 smartphone users aged 16 to 25 across 16 Indian cities. Released ahead of the Infinix GT 50 Pro launch on October 27.

Article Title: Iran's IRGC threatens to cut undersea internet cables in Persian Gulf: What this may mean for internet users across the globe
Article Text:
Who will be impacted if Iran cuts underwater internet cables

Why cutting cables doesn’t mean cutting internet access globally

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) has once again threatened to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz. While the waterway carries only a small share of the world’s internet traffic, damaging its cables will have its impact globally. Notably, the regional impact is likely to be far more severe for countries neighbouring Iran, leaving global internet connectivity largely intact. Yadollah Javani, the Revolutionary Guards’ political deputy, warned this week that vital internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz could be targeted if Iranian infrastructure came under attack.Citing the International Cable Protection Committee (ICPC), a report by Iran International says that five active submarine cable segments pass through the Strait of Hormuz, and together they carry less than 1% of the world’s international bandwidth. It is to be noted that the main data routes linking Europe and East Asia run through the Red Sea. This means that damage to these cables will not have a devastating impact over the internet.TeleGeography says the cables crossing the Strait of Hormuz have been routed through Omani waters because of longstanding political issues and difficult relations with Iran. These cables mainly serve countries in the Persian Gulf, so an attack would be a more immediate threat to regional connectivity than to the wider global internet.Damage to the cables could disrupt international connectivity in Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, though all four have other connections over land. Saudi Arabia depends less on Persian Gulf cable routes, because most of its international bandwidth runs through systems that land on its Red Sea coast.The global internet doesn’t depend on a single network or a single point of failure. Telecom operators use several undersea and land routes to carry data, so if Iran cuts the internet, they can redirect some traffic via other lines. Rerouting may slow speeds, increase delays or disrupt certain services but it doesn’t necessarily cut users off completely.This means the pages may take longer to load, videos may buffer and there may be noticeable delays when refreshing their social media timelines.
Article Summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards have threatened to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway carries only a small share of the world’s internet traffic, but damaging its cables will have its impact globally. The regional impact is likely to be far more severe for countries neighbouring Iran, leaving global internet connectivity largely intact.

Article Title: 80% of India’s insurance buying journey now happens online, Google-McKinsey report claims
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

Why Indians are buying insurance online

“The DICA consumer highlights that purchasing insurance in India is an intricate journey where no single touchpoint or advisor operates in isolation.

When the digital ecosystem directly influences more than 40% of all insurance purchases the online shortlist becomes an important decisive factor. Closing the gap between a consumer's digital evaluation and their offline advisory experience is now the biggest lever for insurance penetration and value creation.

”

Non-metro consumers and salaried professionals lead online research

AI search and YouTube influence insurance decisions

Why insurance buyers still need human assistance

“The emergence of the

DICA consumers

will boost awareness and accessibility in the insurance sector. For insurers, enabling this journey seamlessly across their omnichannel distribution network, like advisors, websites, mobile apps and other digital platforms, can help in building consumer confidence and trust, and thereby increase insurance penetration in India.”

“The future of insurance distribution will not be defined by where customers buy, but by how effectively we connect digital discovery with trusted advice.

When more than 40% of policies are already digitally influenced, the industry's next growth opportunity lies in converting informed intent into meaningful protection.”

Insurance buying in India is increasingly shifting towards online. According to a new study by Google , with McKinsey & Company as its knowledge partner, nearly 80% of India's insurance buying journey now happens online, with consumers using search engines and videos to research policies before approaching an advisor. The report also found that digital research directly influences 40% of health and life insurance sales.‘Decoding the DICA Consumer’ study shows an expanding category of purchasers who shop for insurance providers and filter options online before turning to human assistance to complete the purchase. The findings indicate that digital platforms are influencing insurance decisions, but customers still value a human adviser's input on policy wording, cover, and future financial security.The report identifies these consumers as Digitally Influenced, Closed with Assistance (DICA) buyers. They research policies online, shortlist insurers and then approach advisors to validate their choices and understand policy details.Siddharth Shekar, Director, Google India, said,The report found that 78% of consumers narrow their choices to two or three insurance brands online before speaking to an advisor. More than 50% of consumers continue to prefer their original online shortlist even after consulting an agent.The findings indicate that advisors increasingly need to answer specific questions about coverage, policy exclusions, and service support rather than introduce buyers to insurance brands from scratch.Online insurance research is not limited to consumers in metropolitan cities. According to the study, consumers in leading non-metro cities conduct roughly twice as much online research before purchasing a policy compared with the national average.Salaried professionals aged 25–35 represent the largest demographic driving this digital research. The group also shows higher engagement with comparison tools and policy explainers across age groups.The report calls on insurers to involve consumers at the research stage when they're considering options, rather than only through traditional sales channels.AI-powered search tools and video content are helping consumers understand insurance products. The study found that longer queries account for 18% of insurance searches on Google, reflecting demand for information about specific coverage requirements and complicated policy terms.It also found that 41% of users use AI Overviews to compare options and establish their coverage requirements before approaching an insurer.Video is another important part of the buying journey. Approximately 60% of online insurance researchers use videos during their research, while insurance-related content on YouTube crossed 2.5 billion views in India over the past year. More than 15% of these views occurred on YouTube Connected TV, suggesting insurance research can also involve discussions among household members.Meanwhile, insurance mobile apps are seeing increased engagement for routine activities such as tracking policies and managing claims.Despite the shift towards online research, the study found that fewer than 30% of buyers are comfortable purchasing high-value insurance policies entirely through digital checkout processes.Consumers still seek help understanding policy exclusions, confirming long-term financial security, and getting support during hospital claims. However, the transition from online research to offline sales is not always seamless.More than 40% of buyers said they were frustrated by having to repeat their requirements after being contacted as new leads. More than a third also cited generic sales scripts that did not reflect their specific needs.The report found that offline insurance purchases influenced by online research generate policy premiums approximately 40% higher than traditional sales.Parthanil Ghosh, Managing Director and CEO, HDFC ERGO General Insurance, said,Sumit Madan, Managing Director and CEO, Axis Max Life Insurance, said,The study's findings are based on a survey of 1,039 insurance consumers; aggregated, masked lead-to-conversion analysis across life and health insurers; interviews with industry advisors and distribution platforms; and insights from Google and McKinsey.
Article Summary: Nearly 80% of India's insurance buying journey now happens online. Digital research directly influences 40% of health and life insurance sales. Digital platforms are influencing insurance decisions, but customers still value a human adviser's input on policy wording, cover, and future financial security.

Article Title: When AI valuations correct, India’s case for AI diffusion gets strong
Article Text:
There is No Set Timeline for ‘AGI’ or Generative AI

Industrial AI Policy Push is not a Zero-Sum Game for Public and Private Ecosystems in India

By: Abhivardhan, Managing Partner, Indic Pacific, Sunil Khemka, Program Chair, IEEE Chicago and Technical Convenor (AI & OSS),

, Sanad Arora, Chief Innovation Lead, Indian Society of Artificial Intelligence and Law

Recently, a notable remark from within India’s economic policy establishment observed that if AI-related valuations are subject to market corrections in the advanced economies, then it might be positive for capital inflows in the context of India. His remark should be seen in conjunction with the caution raised in an economic forum that there exists an AI bubble in the US. Naturally, such statements may be seen as defeatist in some ways. However, considering the mainstreaming of AI diffusion across some business-to-business and many business-to-consumer ecosystems, even if the pace is varied across industries, these remarks could make a genuine and unique case of AI Diffusion in late-industrial states, like India.For instance, economists have warned that AI diffusion strains mid-sized enterprises. While some of the “AI Economists” and few other traditional economists argue that the risk of labour or talent replacement remains impeccably high, the real pressure stems from expanding capital disparity. This could be driven by how private equity firms are investing in certain AI firms who then collaborate with certain data rights holders and content publishers.In China, for instance, hedge funds were critical in backing DeepSeek’s success and growth. However, the success of AI labs like DeepSeek has pushed an economically viable chance for the rest of the world including India to pursue alternative options. However, the apocalyptic doom narratives coming from the US exploit actual tension that mid-size firms and startups face. That actual tension, unfortunately, is structural, where mid-market firms are needed to navigate bloated enterprise software costs while maintaining essential human oversight, which in addition - is an unavoidable investment. Nevertheless, as low-cost open models can reduce costs, the vector of “moat” for startups and mid-sized firms unintentionally returns to fundamental research & development, which might explain why AI diffusion is certainly not a lost cause for late industrial states.For late industrial states like India, a more explicit claim has been made that they lack concentrated private equity capital to build proprietary trillion-parameter models like two major AI labs. While from a general R&D perspective it is an issue and one may argue how private and public functionaries support AI and DeepTech initiatives, the infusion of capital should be furthered in those segments and assets, which create a cycle of successive counterparts of the same segments. For instance, a chip design firm in India was acquired by foreign VCs and some commentators argued that it was hurting India’s semiconductor industry and technological sovereignty. Contrary to how they assume, this acquisition made a clear economic case of investing in more Indian talent and resources within India to build more such firms, since the semiconductor economy globally is an interconnected web. However, it does not imply that no sovereign AI ecosystems can be enabled in India at all. Unfortunately, policy reports and sections of a commentariat who argue for and against the “sovereign AI” idea treat the idea as some zero-sum game. The reason they make such flawed assumptions is because they conflate building trillion-parameter models and massive data centres as a measure of geostrategic competition. Since most facets of geostrategic competition are seen as rather zero-sum games, the conflated assumption is cast upon in the case of AI as well. This begs us to ask whether in the pyramid of various “layers” of the AI ecosystem, Indian entities are bound to remain interdependent on all or any layers.Now, one has to understand why this is important. There has been a concerted attempt for years by philosophers, economists and even the prominent AI labs to push the AI doom narrative from a very cut-throat angle of geostrategic competition. It could have made sense to an extent considering the schools of thought around US-China relations that people have developed, and how they particularly look at the economics and certain AI-enabled risks. However, since most of the AI safety discourse focuses on models, and pushes a narrative of AI-associative organised chaos. For instance, Daniel Kokotajlo had created a timeline in a paper called AI 2027, as per which he made technical predictions about the arrival of artificial general intelligence (AGI). While the four major labs kind of diverge on the timelines of AGI, the AI 2027 hypothesis fell flat, since the eagerness to suggest an AGI arrival timeline lacked technical clarity and did not take into account the limitations of the transformers-language models ecosystem.Despite the backlash against AI 2027, various theorists, economists and tech professionals keep proposing timelines around AGI, which centered too much around this US-China competition. Unfortunately, they conflate the persistent promotion of a discourse around US-China AI & compute competition with a rigorous analysis of actual AI evolution & industrial diffusion timelines, which makes no sense.If we look at India’s industrial AI ecosystem developments, there have been enough developments in the semiconductor and electronics industries which show a positive trend. Data centers is another AI ecosystem industry category which is having a calibrative moment nationwide beyond the efforts in Vizag. This leaves us with AI talent, demand issues around AI products & services and AI technical architecture costs beyond cloud / storage and compute. The aftermath of the AI Impact Summit 2026 was interesting for the Indian tech ecosystem, since realisation loomed among India’s startup founders and managers that building AI in India while has challenges around data, funds, and even working culture, emulating a zero-sum approach that is usually pushed in the Silicon Valley is not helpful, irrespective of whether an AI startup intends to sell their products and services in India or beyond. India has immense talent in the AI and analytics space as well as in non-AI industrial sectors, across service & manufacturing sectors whose potential remains untapped, and unfortunately, trapped. In fact, there is a “considerable disconnect in awardees, grants, and the promise vs. delivery of public benefit” as pointed out by economic development specialist Smita Srinivas. This disconnect, often reflects in distorting which technical research and non-AI technical talent to invest in, how to ensure market trust, examining whether a for-profit approach or a not-for-profit approach is logistically sensible for the AI and DeepTech startups building in India. The Indian AI ecosystem must realise that any AI research and diffusion push cannot be treated as a zero-sum game, when in advanced economies, AI diffusion and evolution cycles are conflated with a geostrategic, zero-sum angle of AI diffusion, which might make some of these advanced economies, in WENA countries, especially in North America, lonelier, especially around data, talent & research cooperation. In fact, the shift from traditional SaaS and BPO-like AI delivery models toward the intersection of AI-enabled industrial engineering can also show new horizons. Therefore, the infusion of software engineers and domain specialists can pivot new industry segmentations and opportunities, which is shown by countries like Japan, in their approach towards cooperative AI. It is high time these market distortions are avoided.
Article Summary: Industrial AI Policy Push is not a Zero-Sum Game for Public and Private Ecosystems in India. There is No Set Timeline for ‘AGI’ or Generative AI. There has been a concerted attempt for years by philosophers, economists and even prominent AI labs to push the AI doom narrative.

Article Title: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby is very happy with airlines deal with Starlink, says helping us get customers; Elon Musk responds
Article Text:
Elon Musk Starlink

Elon Musk: 'Starlink moves the needle'

Earnings miss amid higher fuel costs

Ongoing debate with Delta Air Lines

Scott Kirby, the CEO of United Airlines is already noticing customers switch from rival carriers because of its partnership with Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX. According to the remarks made during a CNBC interview and the company's latest earnings discussion, the airline views the rollout as a key competitive advantage. Kirby highlighted that the carrier is expected to cross the milestone of having Starlink installed on more than 50% of its flights this week and that the entire fleet is expected to be equipped with the service by the end of next year, according to a Benzinga report citing the interview. "We already see customers moving from other airlines today," Kirby said when discussing the impact of the onboard internet service. However, he added that it remains unclear whether the benefit will be large enough on its own to help deliver double-digit profit margins.Kirby's comments quickly drew a response from Musk on X. Replying to a post that highlighted the interview, the billionaire wrote: "Starlink moves the needle." The exchange adds to Musk's long-running efforts to promote Starlink's aviation offering as a key differentiator for airlines seeking to improve onboard connectivity. United Airlines calls Starlink a 'tailwind'Speaking during the airline's earnings call, Kirby described Starlink as a "tailwind" for the company and said United has launched a tracking tool that allows passengers to check whether their upcoming flight is equipped with the service.Kirby also expressed confidence that the airline is building a significant lead over competitors."We're on our way to being the only global U.S. airline with Starlink at scale. A lot of new customers are going to try us. It's a huge head start," he said, according to the Benzinga report. The comments suggest that United views onboard connectivity as more than just a passenger convenience feature, seeing it instead as a tool for attracting and retaining travellers.The remarks came as United reported quarterly earnings that fell slightly short of Wall Street expectations. The airline posted earnings of $2.54 per share, below analyst estimates of $2.59 per share. Revenue of $17.875 billion also narrowly missed the consensus forecast of $17.888 billion.United said fuel expenses rose by $1.8 billion year-over-year, driven largely by energy market disruptions linked to the Iran war. During the earnings call, Kirby warned that elevated oil prices could continue to pressure the airline industry over the next year.He also said that between six and 10 U.S. airlines could lose money this year if fuel costs remain high and geopolitical tensions continue to affect energy markets.The latest comments come against the backdrop of an ongoing debate between Musk and Delta Air Lines over inflight internet connectivity. Delta has chosen to deploy Amazon's Project Kuiper-based internet service on its aircraft instead of Starlink. Musk has repeatedly criticised the decision, arguing that airlines risk losing customers by not adopting Starlink's network.In previous comments, Musk warned that Delta could lose passengers because of its decision and even mocked the carrier's onboard connectivity, claiming a flight without reliable internet would be an ideal place to isolate an AI model from online access.With United now publicly stating that Starlink is already helping attract customers from competing airlines, the debate over satellite-powered inflight internet appears set to intensify.
Article Summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby says Starlink is already helping attract customers from rival carriers. Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, is expected to be installed on more than 50% of the airline's flights this week. Kirby's comments quickly drew a response from Musk on X.

Article Title: PHP2Shell: Governments on high alert over critical website flaw; Wikipedia, hospitals, school portals go dark; what users should know
Article Text:
PHP2Shell: AI finds decade-old flaw in software behind 70% of websites; governments take sites offline

PHP is the hidden software behind most websites on the internet

The PHP2Shell flaw lets hackers take over a website without a password

AI found a flaw that had been hiding for over a decade

Most users on the internet can relax, but website owners need to update right away

A large chunk of the internet went offline on Wednesday, and most of it was switched off on purpose. Government websites in the Netherlands, Finland, France and Denmark, along with universities, hospitals and sites as big as Wikipedia, pulled systems down after two serious security flaws were found in PHP. Most people have never heard of PHP, but it is the software running behind roughly 70% of all websites, from news sites and online shops to personal blogs.The flaws, now nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a hacker take over the computer that runs a website without needing a password. They had been hiding in PHP's code for more than a decade, and it took artificial intelligence (AI) to find them. PHP's developers released a fix on October 21, but hackers moved within hours to attack websites that hadn't updated yet. Cyber security agencies in the US and the UK have told website owners to install the fix right away or take their sites offline until they can.The list of affected sites shows how far PHP reaches. The Dutch government's own cyber security agency shut its website as a precaution. Finland took several government online services offline, France's Interior Ministry put all its websites into maintenance mode, and Denmark shut its national school communication platform.In the Netherlands, the Port of Rotterdam, the national football association, several hospitals and the five largest political parties also took their sites down. The Internet Archive went offline briefly, and online forums 4chan and DeviantArt ran into trouble. Even Pokémon Home and Pokémon Champions were taken offline.Some world leaders got involved too. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi posted on X: "We have an urgent request for everyone to take action tonight."The rush makes sense once you see how fast hackers moved. Cloudflare, a company that sits in front of millions of websites to protect them, saw thousands of hacking attempts even before the flaws were made public. CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X that this climbed to tens of thousands within 45 minutes of the announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions by the next morning.Think of a website as having two sides. The side you see is the page in your browser. The side you don't see is a computer, called a server, that builds that page every time you open it. It fetches the right text, images, prices or comments from a database and sends the finished page to your screen. PHP is the language that does this job for a huge share of the web.It has been around since the early 1990s, and it powers WordPress, the tool behind millions of blogs and business websites. It also runs Wikipedia, many government portals, and platforms like Drupal and Joomla that big organisations use to manage their websites. Web tracking firm W3Techs estimates PHP is used by about 69.3% of all websites whose underlying software it can identify.That is why a single flaw in PHP turned into a global problem. Tiffany Farriss, who heads the Drupal Association, told Reuters that any server running a version of PHP from the last 20 years would be vulnerable. "This issue impacts the majority of the internet," she said.PHP is also free and open source, which means anyone can use it. It is looked after by a small non-profit, the PHP Foundation, which has just 13 full-time and part-time engineers maintaining software that much of the internet depends on.Normally, to change a website or access its stored data, you need an administrator login. PHP2Shell skips that step entirely.The two flaws, officially tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are both rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity. In simple terms, a hacker can send a website a carefully crafted request that makes PHP run out of memory and stop halfway through its work. That leaves behind some leftover data in the server. The hacker then sends a second request that makes PHP use that leftover data as if it were normal, and that opens the door to running their own commands on the server.Once inside, a hacker can change what a website shows, plant malicious software that infects visitors, or steal what the server stores. That can include usernames and passwords, digital keys that connect the site to other services, and databases with personal information. A second route even lets hackers peek into the server's short-term memory, where they could catch passwords and login details of other people using the site at the same time.Wiz, one of the firms that found the flaws, showed working attacks on fresh WordPress, Drupal and Joomla websites. It also pointed out that the problem is in PHP itself, so even a basic website with nothing complicated on it can be at risk. Every version of PHP going back more than a decade is affected.The bugs were found by two security firms working separately. Calif says it spotted them on August 1 with the help of an AI model, which OpenAI says was its GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz found them on August 19 using its own AI tool along with Google's Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol.What stands out is that the flaws were not new. PHP's own developers had considered a possible attack along these lines in 2024, but nobody could work out how to make it happen. According to Wiz, turning these bugs into a real attack required so many complex steps that it was at the edge of what human experts could manage. With AI, a single researcher did in a week what would earlier have taken a top team months.The plan was to keep the flaws secret until October 22, giving website companies time to prepare fixes quietly. That plan fell apart when details leaked on online forums and social media on Tuesday. PHP rushed its fix out nearly a day early. Amazon later said its systems saw a hacking attempt on October 17, four days before the public announcement, and nobody yet knows how that attacker found out.OpenAI said in a blog post that the episode shows how AI can uncover security flaws, but also how it can help attackers "rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits." The same kind of AI that found the bug can help hackers study the fix and build an attack in very little time. That is why the window between a fix coming out and attacks starting has shrunk from days to minutes.If you only browse the web, there isn't much you need to do. The flaw targets the servers that run websites, not your phone or laptop. Still, a hacked website can be used to spread malware or steal data, so stay alert for a few weeks. If a service you use asks you to change your password, do it through the official app or website. Be careful with emails or messages about the PHP flaw that ask you to click links or share details, as scammers often use big news like this as bait.If you run a website, even a small blog, check whether it uses PHP. Sites built on Squarespace or Wix are safe, as those platforms don't use PHP. Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, says websites it hosts directly, along with Tumblr, are safe. If you installed WordPress yourself or use a hosting company like GoDaddy, Bluehost or Hostinger, contact your provider to find out when the fix will reach your site.The fixed versions of PHP are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Websites running PHP 8.1 or older won't get a fix at all, because those versions are no longer supported, so they need to move to a newer version. If your site stores customer details or takes payments and you can't confirm it has been fixed, taking it offline for a few hours is the safer choice. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre has also asked organisations that couldn't update quickly to check whether hackers have already left a hidden way back into their systems.Small websites run by individuals and small businesses are the most at risk, since they often lack a technical team and depend on their hosting company to apply fixes.Sigi Goode, a professor of information systems at the Australian National University, told The Guardian where the real danger lies. "The bigger concern is the websites that are not down today," he said. The websites that went dark on Wednesday were the ones taking the threat seriously. The ones still online without the fix are what hackers will be hunting for in the weeks ahead.
Article Summary: Government websites in the Netherlands, Finland, France and Denmark, along with universities, hospitals and sites as big as Wikipedia, pulled systems down. The flaws, now nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a hacker take over the computer that runs a website without needing a password. They had been hiding in PHP's code for more than a decade, and it took artificial intelligence (AI) to find them.

Article Title: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal shares an update on Temple device, writes ‘Temple Batch 01 pre orders open …’
Article Text:
Deepinder Goyal has announced six color options for Temple, his upcoming health wearable device

Hand-made units, three-month delivery timeline

What Temple does

The road to launch

Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has shared a new update on Temple, the hardware venture he has been teasing in recent months, announcing that pre-orders for the first batch of the device will open on November 1. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Goyal wrote, “The wait is over. Temple Batch 01 pre orders open November 1. Each @temple is hand-made to order and delivered to you within three months of your purchase." Along with announcing the pre-order date, Goyal also indicated that the company is taking a measured approach to scaling production. According to Goyal, Temple is following a "grow slow" strategy, with a focus on maintaining quality control and ensuring customers receive a strong experience. "Quality control, and also making sure we serve each customer well. Following the 'grow slow' approach with temple," Goyal said while explaining the company's approach to fulfilling orders.The latest update suggests that Temple's first production batch will be manufactured to order rather than mass-produced. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries expected within three months of purchase.The announcement gives potential buyers their first clear timeline for ordering the device, while also signalling that availability may remain limited during the initial phase as the company prioritises production quality over rapid expansion.It will come in six colours, with Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk marked as limited editions. Temple has not yet announced pricing, the number of devices in the first batch, or the exact date deliveries will begin, and said it would share more information before pre-orders open.Temple is an experimental health-tech wearable developed under a private initiative backed by Goyal. It uses optical sensors to track changes in cerebral blood flow, a metric the company calls BrainFlow. The device tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain. The wearable first drew attention when Goyal appeared on a podcast in early 2026 wearing a small metallic clip-like device on his head.In May, Goyal announced that the first 100 devices were ready to ship to select founding users, including athletes, scientists, doctors, founders and creators. In August, he said the latest version was less than half the size of the one shown earlier, and claimed it was the smallest wearable on the market by volume and the most powerful. Independent reports noted that he gave no hardware specifications or performance data to back that claim. At that time, he said the limited launch edition would ship before the end of 2026. The new three-month delivery window suggests that orders placed from November 1 could reach customers in early 2027.
Article Summary: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has announced pre-orders for Temple will open on November 1. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries expected within three months of purchase. Temple is an experimental health-tech wearable developed under a private initiative backed by Goyal.

Article Title: UltraProlink launches Juice-Up Mag 7 magnetic wireless power bank in India at Rs 3,499
Article Text: Consumer technology accessories brand UltraProlink has expanded its portable charging portfolio with the launch of the Juice-Up Mag 7, a 10,000mAh magnetic wireless power bank designed for smartphones and other compatible devices. The new power bank combines magnetic wireless charging and wired fast charging in a slim 16.5mm form factor. According to the company, the Juice-Up Mag 7 supports up to 15W magnetic wireless charging, 22.5W USB-C Power Delivery (PD) output and 22W PPS fast charging. The product is aimed at users looking for a travel-friendly charging solution for daily commutes, work and travel.The Juice-Up Mag 7 offers magnetic wireless charging with support for 5W, 7.5W, 10W and 15W charging speeds, depending on the connected device. UltraProlink said the magnetic alignment system is designed to work with compatible smartphones, including supported iPhone, Pixel, Samsung and OnePlus devices. For users seeking faster charging speeds, the power bank also supports up to 22.5W USB-C PD charging. The company claims compatible iPhone models can charge from 0% to 50% in 30 minutes through the USB-C port, although actual performance may vary depending on device, battery condition and usage.The device supports multiple charging standards, including PD 3.0, PD 2.0, PPS, QC 3.0, QC 2.0, AFC, PE 2.0, PE 1.1 and SCP, enabling compatibility across a wide range of smartphones and gadgets.Despite housing a 10,000mAh battery, UltraProlink says the Juice-Up Mag 7 measures just 16.5mm thick, making it suitable for carrying in backpacks, laptop bags and travel pouches. The power bank features an integrated LCD display that shows the remaining battery percentage, allowing users to monitor available charge at a glance. The company also highlighted that the 38.5Wh battery capacity meets flight-safe requirements, making it suitable for air travel.UltraProlink said the power bank is BIS certified and manufactured in India. It also incorporates the company's Safety Shield protection system, which includes safeguards against short circuits, overheating, overcurrent and overcharging.The UltraProlink Juice-Up Mag 7 10,000mAh portable power bank is priced at Rs 3,499 and is available through UltraProlink.com and Amazon.in.
Article Summary: The Juice-Up Mag 7 combines magnetic wireless charging and wired fast charging in a slim 16.5mm form factor. The product is aimed at users looking for a travel-friendly charging solution for daily commutes, work and travel. UltraProlink said the magnetic alignment system is designed to work with compatible smartphones, including supported iPhone, Pixel and Samsung devices.

Article Title: After Google renames 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the US; CEO Sundar Pichai says no to US government's request on changing name of Atlantic Ocean; tells: No, no, no, this time I'm not doing it
Article Text:
Trump said he called Google to rename 'Atlantic Ocean' to 'Trump Ocean'

“No, no, no. This time I'm not doing it.” According to Trump, Pichai said, “Oceans are different, sir. They cover a lot of countries. Please don't ask us to do that.”

Trump wants to rename ‘Atlantic Ocean’ to ‘Trump Ocean’

US previously renamed Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario

President Trump, who floated the idea of renaming ‘Atlantic Ocean’ to ‘Trump Ocean’ earlier this month, has once again raised the possibility of renaming the ocean. Speaking at an event recently, Trump revealed that he called Google Maps and asked to rename the Atlantic Ocean. He said that Google CEO Sundar Pichai replied to his proposal saying:This comes months after the tech giant renamed 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the US following an executive order signed by Trump.As mentioned above, Trump first discussed renaming the Atlantic Ocean this month. “We’ve got the gulf. We’ve got a beautiful lake,” Trump said during a rally in Clarksville, Tennessee. “Now, somebody said, you need a river. We need a river. We need an ocean.”He jokingly said that the new name could be in honor of him. “We call it ‘Trump Ocean’ or ‘Ocean of the Americas,’ something like that,” Trump said further adding “Before I get out, I think we should have an ocean. And we need a great river.”Earlier this year, the US administration renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America, sparking diplomatic tensions between the US and Mexico.In August, Trump also renamed Lake Ontario, between New York and Canada, as “Lake America”.After an executive order, Google posted a brief update on its Google Maps blog, noting that it follows the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for its maps. This primarily means that the company has to rename Lake Ontario in Google Maps. Google's update on the name change also made it clear that the change will be only for Google Map users in the US. According to Google, those in the US will only see the new name, which is 'Lake of America'. Meanwhile, Canadians will continue to see the 'Lake Ontario' label. In the rest of the world, Lake Ontario will take precedence, but Lake America will also be there in parentheses. Apple followed the suit renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America on Maps for US users.
Article Summary: Trump said he called Google to rename 'Atlantic Ocean' to 'Trump Ocean' He said that Google CEO Sundar Pichai replied saying: “Oceans are different, sir. They cover a lot of countries. Please don't ask us to do that” This comes months after the tech giant renamed 'Lake Ontario' to ‘Lake America' in the US.

Article Title: Angry protestors 'interrupt' Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's event in Berlin, shout: 'What about technology found in Russian drones, those were ...'
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

Nvidia CEO on 'Berlin protests'

Nvidia chips 'found' in Russian drones

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote address at the company’s GTC conference in Berlin was interrupted by protestors on Wednesday morning. Minutes into the keynote, hecklers stood on chairs in the auditorium displaying a Greenpeace banner reading, "Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!" While the disruption was largely missed by the official livestream, attendee footage posted to Twitter captured demonstrators pressing Huang directly."Jensen, what about the technology that was found in Russian drones? Those were Nvidia chips. What are you doing about that?" one demonstrator shouted across the hall. "What are you doing about that? What are you doing about the environmental destruction?" The demonstration occurred during Nvidia’s three-day GTC Berlin event, running from October 20–22, which features developer sessions, executive panels, and industry talks alongside Huang’s opening address.The Nvidia CEO too made a small mention of the protests on stage, jokingly, he said, "All important issues, but let me get through my keynote." Huang remarked this before resuming the presentation.The outburst follows reports detailing the discovery of Nvidia components—specifically within Russia's S-71 "Monochrome" weapon, which relies on consumer-grade Jetson Orin modules for autonomous targeting—as well as in cruise missiles deployed against Ukraine.Some reports in August identified an autonomous Russian AI drone powered by Jetson Orin hardware as the cause of three civilian deaths in Ukraine, marking the first documented case of its kind.A Russian Molniya drone allegedly carrying an Nvidia Jetson Orin module crashed and killed three civilians at a gas station in Zaporizhzhia in August after choosing its final target without a human pilot. A New York Times investigation cited Ukrainian air defense commanders, drone experts, and the forensic team that examined the wreckage, as source of their report.Nvidia confirmed to the New York Times that modules photographed in the recovered drones were Jetson Orin minicomputers, hardware that sells for a few hundred dollars. "Our Jetson Orin modules are consumer-grade products sold to students, developers, and startups for a wide range of beneficial applications," an Nvidia spokesperson reportedly told Tom's Hardware.The statement added, "They are not available in Russia and are not designed for military purposes. Pre-owned Jetsons are available through many reseller channels. Although we cannot track products after they are sold, if we determine that any customer is violating U.S. export controls, we will take appropriate action."
Article Summary: Protestors interrupted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's keynote address at GTC conference in Berlin. Demonstrators stood on chairs displaying a Greenpeace banner reading, "N Nvidia, clean up your dirty business!" The outburst follows reports detailing the discovery of Nvidia components in Russian drones and cruise missiles.

Article Title: Anthropic introduces Claude Duet AI agent app for professionals: Features, availability and more
Article Text:
Anthropic introduces Claude Duet AI agent app for professional

Claude Duet: What can the new AI agent do

Claude Duet supports thousands of business tools

Claude Duet availability and subscription details

Anthropic has introduced Claude Duet, a new AI-powered app designed to help professionals and small business owners manage their work with less manual effort. The app can monitor connected accounts, flag tasks that need attention, prepare reports and handle work in the background, even when users step away from their devices. Unlike a chatbot that waits for instructions, Claude Duet can proactively alert users about important updates and help complete tasks across different apps. The research preview is now open through a waitlist for users in the US with Claude Pro and Max subscriptions, with access available on iOS, Android and the web.“We built Claude Duet for professionals and small business owners with more on their plates than they can track,” Anthropic said.According to the company, Claude Duet is designed to help users manage busy schedules and prioritise important work. Each morning, it can send a short summary of key items across connected apps. It then checks those accounts every few hours and sends notifications when something needs attention.Users can also assign tasks, ranging from scheduling meetings and drafting emails to building dashboards, preparing financial forecasts and developing web apps.The app is built around Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 model and is designed to decide which tasks need immediate attention and when it should ask users for guidance.One of the key features of Claude Duet is its ability to continue working when users are away from their phones or computers. The app uses a virtual machine with its own browser to carry out tasks in the background. Users can send instructions through text or voice in a single ongoing conversation and receive a notification when a task is complete or requires their review.Claude Duet also carries over existing memory, skills and connected apps from a user's Claude account, which Anthropic says should make setup easier.Anthropic says Claude Duet is designed to ask for permission before taking important actions on a user's behalf. The app can read messages, draft replies and prepare work independently. However, it must seek approval before sending messages, making payments, signing documents or deleting anything.Some actions, such as trading securities or transferring money between accounts, are not allowed even with user approval.The company has also introduced additional safeguards to protect sensitive information. According to Anthropic, the system is designed to block requests to share highly sensitive details, such as credit card numbers and government identification. Other sensitive information, including health and personal financial details, can be shared only when users have explicitly instructed the app to do so.Claude Duet can connect with more than 6,000 connectors and plugins through the Claude Marketplace, allowing it to work with tools used by businesses. These integrations can help users find missed messages in Gmail and Slack, track unpaid invoices through QuickBooks or Stripe, prepare payroll in Gusto, draft job postings for LinkedIn and manage customer information in HubSpot.It can also help businesses create marketing campaigns using Canva and manage Shopify stores. Anthropic says support for a richer visual editor for Shopify storefronts is coming soon.Users can also make business purchases through Link, Stripe's digital wallet, and use Shop Pay for online checkout. Support for signing in to websites through saved 1Password logins is planned for a future update.Anthropic has opened a research preview of Claude Duet through a waitlist, starting with Claude Pro and Max subscribers in the US. The app is available as a standalone offering on iOS and Android, as well as through claude.ai.During the preview, Claude Duet shares the same usage limits as the user's existing Claude plan. Background checks and complex tasks can consume those limits more quickly than ordinary conversations.
Article Summary: Claude Duet is designed to help professionals and small business owners manage their work with less manual effort. The app can monitor connected accounts, flag tasks that need attention, prepare reports and handle work in the background. Unlike a chatbot that waits for instructions, Claude Duet can proactively alert users about important updates and help complete tasks.

Article Title: Google co-founder Larry Page is the richest tech titan to leave California ahead of Billionaire's tax vote: How his exit may dent state’s $100 billion tax target
Article Text:
Moving entities to Delaware and buying big in Miami

The $29 billion dent in Prop 40’s target

With Californians set to vote in just a few weeks on Proposition 40 – a measure proposing a one-time 5% wealth tax on the state's billionaires – Google co-founder Larry Page has emerged as the wealthiest tech titan to sever ties with the state should the measure pass. His departure is likely to deal a significant blow to California's revenue projections as he will be the richest techie to leave the state. The initiative specifically targets billionaires who were state residents as of January 1, 2026. While a few prominent executives, such as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, have stated they are "perfectly fine" with the proposal, multiple ultra-wealthy residents chose to exit before the January deadline.Chief among them is the 53-year-old Page. Holding an estimated net worth of $292 billion, Page had deep roots in California spanning decades, Fortune reported, adding that had he remained a California resident past the cutoff date, he would have owed an estimated $15 billion under the one-time tax levy.State filings have revealed that Page began unwinding his operational and personal presence in California late last year.According to an analysis of corporate records reported by Fortune, Page’s family office, Koop, was transferred out of California and officially incorporated in Delaware in late December. Multiple associated entities, including Flu Lab LLC, One Aero and Oceankind, followed the same route, moving their registrations from California to Delaware during the same month.Simultaneously, Page redirected significant capital toward luxury real estate on the East Coast. The Wall Street Journal reported that Page acquired two premier estates in Miami for a combined $173.4 million, which includes Coconut Grove Estate ($101.5 million, 11,855-square-foot property) and a neighboring parcel purchased for $71.9 million.The departures of top-tier billionaires have already weakened the potential financial yield of the ballot measure. Prop 40 was projected to generate roughly $100 billion for the state. However, according to an estimate by Fortune, just four departed tech leaders – Larry Page, Sergey Brin, Peter Thiel and former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick – would have collectively owed approximately $29 billion. Their relocations before the residency cutoff mean the state has effectively lost out on more than a quarter of the measure's total projected revenue pool before ballots are even counted.Elon Musk, the richest person in the world, moved to Texas in 2020. Meanwhile, Jeff Bezos who recently but briefly secured the second richest person spot, departed Seattle for Miami in late 2023, eventually selling his Hunts Point home for a record $63 million to live in a $237 million Miami compound with his wife, Lauren Sánchez Bezos.
Article Summary: Google co-founder Larry Page is the wealthiest tech titan to sever ties with the state should the measure pass. His departure is likely to deal a significant blow to California's revenue projections. The initiative specifically targets billionaires who were state residents as of January 1, 2026.

Article Title: Patch or go offline, say security agencies in the US, UK and Europe to companies as two critical bugs in PHP put millions of websites at risk
Article Text:
Representative Image

FBI to companies in America: Follow these steps right away

UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to companies: Update to the latest version

European Union's CERT-EU to organisations: Patch affected assets immediately

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think government websites should have gone offline as a precaution? Yes, it's the right move. No, it causes unnecessary disruption. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Several security agencies across the world have sent out an alarming warning that two critical holes have been found in PHP. The critical bugs allow hackers to run code on almost any server running the PHP language. For those unaware, PHP is a server-side programming language widely used for web applications. It is said to power roughly 70% of the websites on the internet. Reports suggest that the details on two critical-severity PHP vulnerabilities named PHP2Shell have been leaked online ahead of scheduled coordinated disclosure and official patches. Public reporting calls the vulnerabilities PHP2Shell, suggesting that attackers could exploit them to obtain shells on vulnerable servers.Following the disclosure, government websites in several parts of Europe, UK and some in the US went offline. The Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities. Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider Valtori said that the government public network services had been taken offline "as a precautionary measure." France's Interior Ministry said it had placed all of its websites into preventive maintenance.Here's what security agencies across the world are telling companies to do to protect their websites and businesses.The US National Security Agency told companies to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline. The flaws "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," the NSA said in a statement. Attackers could use them to take over web servers without needing a password.The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) urged organizations to take the following steps now:* If an immediate update is not feasible it is recommended that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.* Immediately update affected PHP installations following the guidance on PHP webite . Inventory where PHP runs in your environment, prioritizing internet-facing systems and vendor products that bundle PHP.* Monitor web servers for suspicious activity, including PHP processes unexpectedly launching command shells or downloading files. Ensure appropriate process-monitoring capabilities are in place to help identify potential exploitation.* If you find signs of compromise, isolate affected systems, preserve your web server and PHP logs, and report it to your local FBI field office. Those reports help us identify the actors involved and warn other organizations before they become victims.Organisations using any version of PHP are affected and all organisations are highly encouraged to update to the latest fixed version. Organisations using older versions of PHP are highly encouraged to update to a fully supported version. The NCSC recommends following vendor best practice advice in the mitigation of vulnerabilities. The NCSC highly encourages organisations to follow these priority actions:* Identify systems running PHP across your infrastructure, prioritising internet-facing systems. As all versions may be affected, do not limit discovery to outdated PHP versions; identify PHP installations generally and assess their exposure to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.Continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP as a component. Apply relevant updates as they become available.* Update to the latest version of PHP and continue to monitor for future updates.* Apply the additional hardening steps provided by the PHP Team.* If you are unable to update to a version with the security update applied, the PHP Team have provided temporary mitigations.* If you are unable to apply the temporary mitigations, or applying them would take too long, you should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated.* If you are unable to update, or disable, the system immediately then you should assess the system for any evidence of compromise prior to your upgrade or mitigation and look for backdoors installed by an attacker. If you are not confident in your ability to do this yourselves then you can get assistance from an NCSC-assured Cyber Incident Response provider.* Continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP. NCSC-NL have published an inventory list of software products with a PHP dependency potentially affected by the vulnerabilities.The EU's CERT-EU offered similar advice, telling operators to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied" where remediation could not happen at once. In a release on its website, it says, "CERT-EU strongly recommends updating all affected PHP installations as soon as possible to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 [4]."* Distribution packages: Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance. Check with your vendor for updated packages.* End-of-life versions (PHP 8.1 and older): Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor or upgrade to a supported version. Because of the severity, the PHP security team has also published minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 for organisations that build from source or have no LTS vendor.rpms.remirepo.net users: This volunteer-maintained repository will not have updates on release day. The PHP team urges users to switch to distribution packages or build from source.* Where immediate patching is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing resources from public networks until the fix is applied and verified.
Article Summary: Two critical holes have been found in the server-side programming language PHP. The US National Security Agency told companies to patch immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline. The flaws "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," the NSA said. Government websites in several parts of Europe, UK and some in the US went offline.

Article Title: Judge orders Meta to pay $25 billion in trial related to 8-year-old data privacy scandal
Article Text:
Meta

Internal inquiry was ‘Willfully Ineffective’

A New Mexico state court has ordered Facebook-parent company Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty following a long legal battle stemming from the Cambridge Analytica data privacy scandal from nearly a decade ago. The judgment, revealed in a court filing on Wednesday (October 21), follows a September verdict by a jury in a Santa Fe courthouse. Jurors found the social media giant liable for deceiving New Mexico residents regarding how it gathers and safeguards personal data, as well as how it stops harmful content from spreading across its platforms.The jury determined that Meta committed more than 43 million individual violations of the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act, each subject to a statutory civil fine of up to $5,000. However, the final penalty amount was left to judicial discretion. The ruling revealed that while the state was initially awarded $219.5 billion, the court reduced the ultimate penalty to $25 billion. In his filing, New Mexico District Court Judge Francis Mathew delivered a rebuke of the company's past actions and internal practices, arguing that the maximum fine per violation was fully justified.“The extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership, the size of New Mexico audiences reached, and the clear intentional and systematic nature of Facebook’s repeated misstatements established in the trial record support the highest level of penalty allowed by the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act - $5,000 per violation found by the jury,” Judge Mathew wrote.Judge Mathew also ordered that the penalty will accrue interest at an annual rate of 15% until the judgment is settled in full.The ruling pointed out that Facebook failed to live up to its public commitments following the 2018 Cambridge Analytica revelations, in which the political consultancy improperly gathered data belonging to an estimated 87 million users. Judge Mathew concluded that the tech firm “did not conduct the comprehensive investigation that it promised.”Meta previously attempted to clear away nationwide litigation tied to the Cambridge Analytica fallout. In August, the tech giant agreed to an overarching $17 billion multi-state settlement with a coalition of state attorneys general in a broader federal lawsuit centered on child safety and mental health.However, as New Mexico chose not to join that nationwide pact, the state's independent Cambridge Analytica lawsuit proceeded directly to trial in September. The original complaint was initiated in 2021 by former New Mexico Attorney General Hector Balderas, with current Attorney General Raúl Torrez directing the courtroom trial to its conclusion.
Article Summary: A New Mexico state court has ordered Facebook-parent company Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty following a long legal battle. The judgment follows a September verdict by a jury in a Santa Fe courthouse. Jurors found the social media giant liable for deceiving New Mexico residents regarding how it gathers and safeguards personal data.

Article Title: Decades-old flaw in PHP discovered by Google, OpenAI AI tools forces government and public websites to go offline globally
Article Text:
Representative image

Flaw impacting the ‘backbone of the web’

Flaw discovered through Artificial Intelligence

Government portals, municipal networks and public institutions across Europe and other regions went offline on Wednesday (October 21) after researchers disclosed critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a foundational programming language that powers a vast portion of the global web. The disclosures prompted emergency responses from IT teams worldwide, with operators taking critical servers offline as a defensive shield to prevent malicious intrusions before security updates could be deployed. Developers of the open-source PHP language published urgent security fixes for flaws that had remained buried inside the language’s codebase for years. Issuing an emergency advisory, the team stated that all site owners and server administrators are “encouraged to update immediately.”With tech security firms warning that malicious actors have already begun targeting unpatched setups, the disclosure triggered an immediate “race to exploit.” As fixes are now public, analysts warned that artificial intelligence (AI) tools could allow hackers to reverse-engineer the vulnerability with minimal effort.“Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale. With AI this is no longer a barrier,” noted cybersecurity firm Wiz, warning that AI-assisted attacks could lead to the mass compromise of unprotected web servers across the internet.Created in the early 1990s as “Personal Home Page,” PHP has evolved into one of the core backbones of modern internet infrastructure. When a user visits a webpage, servers running PHP assemble the text, media and code before serving it to the browser. According to web analytics tracker W3Techs, PHP underpins roughly 75% of all websites where the server-side language can be identified.“All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable. This issue impacts the majority of the Internet,” said Tiffany Farriss, interim chief executive of the Drupal Association.Due to this widespread footprint, national cyber agencies across Britain, Europe, Japan and Australia issued advisories directing web administrators to install updates immediately or take public-facing pages offline.The underlying security flaw sat hidden in the software codebase for over a decade. In a technical brief, Alphabet-owned cybersecurity firm Wiz revealed that human researchers would have found it extraordinarily complex to locate and exploit through conventional testing. Instead, the vulnerability was surfaced through advanced AI tooling:Wiz discovered the flaw using Wiz Atlas, its autonomous vulnerability discovery system, working alongside Google ’s Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz collaborated with the PHP core developer team, OpenAI and security firm Calif to verify the bug and confirm remediation patches.Early mitigation protocols were shared with cloud and infrastructure operators, including Google Cloud, Cloudflare, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft, Automattic (operator of WordPress.com), Fastly, Akamai, Imperva and Vercel.
Article Summary: Vulnerabilities in the open-source PHP programming language have been disclosed. The language underpins 75% of all websites where the server-side language can be identified. The underlying security flaw sat hidden in the software codebase for over a decade. The disclosure triggered an immediate “race to exploit”

Article Title: In 2024, Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez gave $3 million to Habitat for Humanity Maui; the donation backed affordable housing and efforts to repair and rebuild homes after the island's devastating fires
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez's $3 million donation to Habitat for Humanity Maui

Maui wildfires increased the need for affordable housing and home repairs

How Habitat for Humanity Maui supports local families

The role of private giving in the recovery effort

When wildfires tore through Maui in August 2023, the damage extended well beyond the buildings reduced to ash. Families lost their homes, neighbourhoods were disrupted and the shortage of affordable housing became harder to manage. For residents already struggling with the cost of living on the Hawaiian island, finding somewhere to live became an additional concern. As reported by Maui Now, in October 2024, Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez donated $3 million to Habitat for Humanity Maui, providing support for affordable housing programmes and work to repair and rebuild homes affected by the fires. The donation highlights how private philanthropy can strengthen local housing organisations and support long-term recovery for families displaced by natural disasters.Habitat for Humanity Maui announced the contribution on 29 October 2024. The gift was among the largest the organisation had received in its history, according to the announcement, and came as the island continued to deal with the consequences of the wildfires and an existing shortage of affordable homes.The funding was intended to help the organisation expand its housing work, including construction and repair projects for local families.Some of the money would go towards rebuilding homes damaged by the fires, while other support would help more residents access homeownership.The donation also gave the organisation additional resources to increase its building capacity. For a community facing substantial housing needs, the ability to undertake more projects can affect how many families receive assistance and how quickly homes can be repaired or built.The wildfires that struck Maui in August 2023 caused widespread destruction, particularly in the historic town of Lahaina. Homes and businesses were lost, and many residents had to leave areas where they had lived for years. The disaster placed further pressure on an island where housing costs were already a persistent concern.Recovery involved more than clearing damaged sites and replacing buildings. Residents also needed access to housing they could afford while rebuilding plans moved forward. For households on lower incomes, returning to the island or remaining close to their communities could be difficult when available accommodation was limited and expensive.Habitat for Humanity Maui's work covered both the construction of homes and the repair of existing properties. The Bezos and Sanchez contribution was intended to strengthen those efforts, helping the organisation respond to the needs of families whose housing circumstances had been affected by the fires.As reported, Habitat for Humanity Maui has worked on affordable housing on the island for more than 25 years. Its programmes are designed to help households who might struggle to secure suitable housing through the conventional market.The organisation builds and repairs homes for qualifying families using a model that does not charge interest or generate a profit on the housing provided. According to its published description, it serves households earning between 25% and 80% of Maui County's median income.The October 2024 donation was intended to support this existing work while allowing the organisation to reach more households. It was not limited to a single rebuilding project, with the stated uses also covering wider affordable housing programmes and access to homeownership.The contribution formed part of a wider effort to address Maui's housing needs following the fires. Local organisations, public agencies and private donors have all had roles in the island's recovery, although the scale of demand has meant that housing remains a long-term concern rather than a problem that can be resolved through one funding announcement.For Habitat for Humanity Maui, the $3 million gift offered additional resources for its construction and repair work. The organisation said the money would help it serve more families at a time when demand for safe, affordable homes remained high.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez donated $3 million to Habitat for Humanity Maui in October 2024. The gift was among the largest the organisation had received in its history. Some of the money would go towards rebuilding homes damaged by the fires, while other support would help more residents access homeownership.
