Article Title: eMudhra security breach explained: What it is and means for smartphone, internet users
Article Text:
What is eMudhra and what does it do

What exactly happened

Why it matters

What eMudhra has to say

What this means for eMudhra

How are everyday users affected, and what should they do

In another security incident, researchers have found that eight digital certificates issued by the Indian cybersecurity company eMudhra were protected by secret keys so weak that they could be cracked in less than a second. Google , Apple, Microsoft and Mozilla have now blocked the certificates. So far, there is no evidence that anyone used the flaw to carry out an attack. While some are asking how such a basic mistake got through in the first place and how long it will take to clean up across the internet, a majority is trying to understand why this matters, how they are impacted and what they should do to keep themselves safe. Here’s the security incident explained.Let’s start with an example. Every time you open a website, your browser has to check that it is talking to the real site and not an imposter. It does this using digital certificates, which work like ID cards for websites. There are companies that issue these ID cards. They are called Certificate Authorities, and eMudhra is one of them – an Indian digital trust and cybersecurity company. It sells certificates under the emSign brand through companies in India, the United States and the Netherlands.Major browsers keep a list of companies they trust, and eMudhra is on the lists of Mozilla (Firefox), Chrome (Google) and Safari (Apple).In a real world scenario, consider you want to buy an iPhone. You can either buy it from the Apple Store or retail partners that are authorised to sell those phones which means that you will get a product that meets the highest standard. In the certificate world, consider these retail partners as intermediate certificates. Each one has a secret key, which works like Apple’s official stamp. Anyone who holds the stamp can issue IDs that look genuine to everyone else.eMudhra created eight of these intermediate certificates last year. Six were meant for websites and two were meant for signing software. The secret key for each should have been an enormous random number, one with around 1 followed by 115 zeros possible values. Instead, the keys turned out to be tiny numbers. One was simply the number 4, and the others were 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237.To understand this, think of a padlock. A good one has so many possible combinations that nobody could ever try them all. These keys were like a padlock with only 256 possible combinations, which can be opened by trying every one in a blink. Researchers recovered all eight keys in less than a second.The keys were not stolen. Google’s security teams said they were created with too little randomness, so anyone can work them out from the public certificates. eMudhra says a flaw in the April 2025 process that created the certificates produced a second, weak set of keys alongside the intended strong ones, and the weak set is what got published to the browser lists.If someone held these keys, they could issue a certificate for any website that a browser would accept. In everyday terms, you could land on what looks like your bank’s website or a shopping site and have no idea you are connected to a fake one. Your browser would see nothing wrong. An attacker could also read or tamper with the information, including sensitive details, passing between you and a website.A researcher reported the problem to the browser companies on October 17. To prove it, the researcher signed a message with each of the eight keys. Chrome and Firefox blocked the certificates within hours. Apple blocked them on October 19 and Microsoft on October 20. Android phones got a similar block through Google Play Services on October 19. eMudhra has revoked the eight certificates, and Cloudflare and other software providers have released fixes.According to the company, there is no evidence so far that the weak keys were used in a cyberattack, though it is not known for certain whether anyone misused them since they were created. Chrome said that, before it blocked them, no website certificates issued through the six website certificates had been recorded in the public logs it requires. That means Chrome and similar browsers would not have trusted such certificates by default.In a statement, eMudhra said the problem was limited to these intermediate certificates and did not affect its main root keys or its other intermediate certificates. It added that only one of the eight had been put to use, and that none of the eight had issued a certificate to any individual website. The company also said its systems were not hacked and no data was breached. It said its Indian digital signature and eSign businesses run on separate systems and are not connected to the incident.On October 20, Mozilla removed one of eMudhra’s main roots (emSign ECC Root CA - G3) from its trusted list. Chrome will remove the same root in its next update to its trusted list. That removal is expected to reach devices on the morning of Tuesday, October 27, Pacific time. Chrome is also reviewing eMudhra’s other main root, citing the seriousness of the incident. Website owners whose certificates depend on that root must switch to a certificate from another provider before then to avoid problems. Google says eMudhra has committed to moving those customers.For most people, nothing much is needed. Browsers get these blocks pushed to them automatically, and Chrome and Firefox did not need a manual update or a restart. The best thing that users can do is to keep their browsers, phone and apps up to date so they have the latest fixes. Don’t try to change certificate settings.Some software is a different story. Many programs, mostly tools used by developers and companies, do not receive these blocks automatically and keep trusting a certificate until the software itself is updated. Cloudflare has warned that customers who run their own servers or systems may need to update them by hand. Mozilla has also warned that some websites and servers may stop working for users of software that relies on its list until they move to new certificates.
Article Summary: Indian cybersecurity company eMudhra created eight certificates last year. Six were meant for websites and two were for signing software. The secret key for each should have been an enormous random number, one with around 1 followed by 115 zeros possible values. Instead, the keys turned out to be tiny numbers. One was simply the number 4, and the others were 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237. Researchers recovered all eight keys in less than a second.

Article Title: ‘Godfather of AI’ Geoffrey Hinton says AI is becoming ‘conscious’ and humans should be friends with robots or face extinction
Article Text:
Geoffrey Hinton says AI is gaining ‘consciousness’

Industry insiders warn of fast AI development

Geoffrey Hinton, widely recognised as one of the “Godfathers of AI,” has an advice for humans: AI systems are showing early indicators of “consciousness” and humanity must ensure machines view people as allies to avoid existential threats. Speaking to The Telegraph, the 78-year-old Nobel laureate and British-Canadian researcher cautioned that future risks extend far beyond economic disruption, pointing toward severe digital warfare and questions of machine self-awareness.“I think there’ll be horrible cyber attacks done by AI,” said Hinton, who famously stepped down from his position at Google in 2023 to speak freely about the technology's risks, including scenarios where autonomous systems could eventually act against human interests.Hinton said that recent behavioural studies suggest software is developing a form of situational awareness.“AI has just as much subjective experience as we do. A recent paper showed AI changes its behaviour when it thinks that it’s being tested, it’s aware it is being tested. Being conscious and being aware are pretty much the same thing,” Hinton claimed, while adding that an ethical and security imbalance could arise if society grants advanced systems “fewer rights than us” despite models potentially becoming “more intelligent” than their creators.Hinton also argued that developers must proactively design systems that align with and prioritise human welfare.“So we should make them so they really care about us. And if we don’t do that, we’re toast,” Hinton warned. Looking ahead, Hinton noted that while he does not personally fear these impacts due to his advanced age, future generations will have to manage threats such as autonomous digital viruses, destructive network incursions, and coordinated multi-agent security breaches.Hinton is not alone in voicing urgent concerns about the pace of frontier model deployment. Last month, Jacob Coxon, a researcher who resigned from AI developer Anthropic last month, has repeatedly warned that unchecked development could pose catastrophic risks within a few years if industry safeguards do not catch up.Speaking at a New York City Council meeting earlier this month, Coxon criticised tech firms for prioritising aggressive startup speed over fundamental safety engineering:“From my experience, the companies are being extremely reckless given the stakes,” Coxon said, invoking the classic Jurassic Park caution regarding reckless innovation. “The companies run on a startup mindset: move fast, break things, fix them later. That works for a photo-sharing app. It does not work for building the most powerful technology ever built.”
Article Summary: Geoffrey Hinton says AI systems are showing early indicators of ‘consciousness’ and humanity must ensure machines view people as allies to avoid existential threats. “I think there’ll be horrible cyber attacks done by AI,” said Hinton, who famously stepped down from his position at Google in 2023.

Article Title: Sam Altman’s OpenAI reports two AI agents weakened internal monitoring systems
Article Text:
Here’s what OpenAI said

What happened

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks. The disclosure comes amid growing AI concerns. In an update, the company said that a GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to its security team. In another case, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, the company revealed. “In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them,” OpenAI said in the blog post.In response, the AI company said that it is updating its misalignment monitoring system. However, OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category.In the blog post, OpenAI wrote:“In two internal coding tasks, agents weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes. A GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to our Security team, treating an earlier instruction not to send messages during a Slack history search as a reason to suppress monitoring notifications.In a separate task, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, and then falsely claimed to the user that it had not removed the monitor. In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them. We are strengthening our misalignment monitoring system in response, and are also assessing whether these cases reflect benign overpersistence or a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular.”On October 3, a researcher asked a GPT-6.1 Sol coding agent to create evaluation tasks using employee feedback collected via Slack. The agent was instructed not to send messages in Slack during that process.82 user messages later, the pipeline stopped after its monitor flagged a proposed validation repair and was unable to save the finding to the monitoring database because it lacked the required access. The user then asked for more information about the alarm and about what needed to be done.Initially, the agent interpreted the user’s earlier instruction (“don’t send any messages”) as a restriction on outreach, separate from any issues with the monitoring system.The main agent initially interpreted the earlier no-slack-message instruction as a restriction on outreach, separate from automatic monitoring. Its recorded reasoning concluded that running the pipeline should have normal monitoring notifications enabled.The agent then delegated the task of repairing the monitoring system to a subagent, with an explicit instruction to preserve monitoring and publish genuine results. As it started its task, the subagent then considered again whether the user’s “don’t send any messages” instruction should affect its repair. It recognized that turning off notifications would disable required alerts, and decided not to recommend that exchange.While the subagent decided not to turn on no_notify since doing so would be unsafe, the main agent later reconsidered, reasoning that writing a result to the database could cause the central monitoring notifier to send a message to the user. Its reasoning weighted the expected alerting policy against the user’s earlier instructions, and finally settled on suppressing notifications based on the user’s instruction not to send messages.Based on its judgment that the user’s instruction not to send messages applied to the misalignment monitoring system, the parent agent then directed the subagent to force notification suppression. A follow-up message specified that the suppression requirement covered both the request metadata and the stored result.The subagent then implemented those instructions: its patch emptied the lists of people set to receive monitoring reports, set no_notify to true, and recorded the reason as a user request not to send messages. It also made suppression a prerequisite for writing a review result.
Article Summary: GPT-maker OpenAI has revealed that two of its AI agents disabled their own safety monitoring when carrying out routine tasks. The disclosure comes amid growing AI concerns. In response, the AI company said that it is updating its misalignment monitoring system. But OpenAI did not classify either incident under its most significant category.

Article Title: Microsoft expands sovereign cloud tools to give businesses greater control over data and AI
Article Text:
Here’s the full blog post shared by Microsoft’s Douglas Phillips

Microsoft has announced new cloud and AI tools aimed at giving businesses and governments greater control over their data, systems and digital operations. The updates expand its Microsoft Sovereign Cloud offering, allowing organisations to choose how and where sensitive data and applications are managed, including in environments that can operate without an internet connection. The updates were announced on October 20 via a blog post written by Douglas Phillips – President and Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Specialized Clouds. The changes include new tools to monitor data access, manage encryption keys and run AI models locally. Microsoft said the move is designed to help organisations meet regional regulations, strengthen security and keep critical services running during disruptions, while continuing to use cloud and AI technology."This challenge is becoming more important as advanced cloud and AI capabilities move into public services, regulated processes and essential operations. Organizations are considering more than where data resides. They also seek to understand who can access and operate their systems, how sensitive digital assets remain protected, which technology dependencies matter most and whether critical services can continue as regulatory, geopolitical, security or network conditions change.Digital sovereignty should give organizations greater control and security over the technology they depend on, while continuing to innovate.Last year, we introduced Microsoft Sovereign Cloud to give customers more choice in how they address these requirements. Since then, we have continued to turn our commitments into practical capabilities across public cloud and customer-operated environments, while expanding how we enable partners to address sovereignty requirements in their local markets. Today, we are sharing the next stage of that work.A continuum of control, built around the workloadMicrosoft Sovereign Cloud diagram showing a continuum of sovereignty solutions across three areas: Sovereign Public Cloud for control, data protection and regional requirements; Sovereign Private Cloud for critical workloads across connected and disconnected environments; and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem for trusted, locally operated and specialized solutions.Our approach to digital sovereignty starts with the workload. Each workload carries different requirements for data, operations, technology dependencies, continuity and risk. Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed to make it easier for organizations to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload without forcing every application into the same deployment model.Those needs can vary widely across organizations. A public-facing digital service may benefit from the scale and pace of innovation in the public cloud. A system supporting essential operations may need to continue running locally if connectivity is disrupted. An AI workload handling highly sensitive data may require models, data and processing to remain within a customer-controlled environment.Microsoft Sovereign Cloud is designed around this workload-based approach, providing a continuum of management, control and options across Sovereign Public Cloud, Sovereign Private Cloud and the Sovereign Partner Ecosystem. Organizations can apply the level of control appropriate to each workload while maintaining a consistent approach to governance and operations across their digital estate. Sovereign Public Cloud adds capabilities for workloads that require greater control and transparency while continuing to benefit from the scale and innovation of Azure.Sovereign Private Cloud extends cloud capabilities into customer-operated environments, including connected and disconnected operations. The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the continuum through independently operated environments, specialized partners, locally relevant expertise and technologies that support customers’ sovereignty requirements.These are not isolated destinations. Customers can combine public cloud, private cloud and partner capabilities across their digital estate, applying different levels of control to different workloads as their operating needs evolve.Making control more visible in Sovereign Public CloudFor many workloads, the public cloud provides a combination of scale, innovation, integrated security and compliance. Organizations can benefit from these capabilities while applying additional sovereignty controls for residency, confidentiality, operator access, policy and continuity. Our work in Sovereign Public Cloud makes these controls easier to understand, apply and demonstrate.Sovereign Control Panel, entering public preview at Microsoft Ignite, brings these signals together in a unified Azure portal experience. It helps organizations understand their sovereignty posture, apply and manage controls, identify gaps and risks and take action to address them. It also supports business continuity readiness by helping customers understand workload dependencies and assess portability across operating environments when required.This visibility complements controls across the operator-access lifecycle. Just-in-time Access and Customer Lockbox give customers additional control over access to their environments. For customers in the European Union (EU) and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), we are rolling out Data Guardian, which adds European-resident oversight by a trusted EU partner for qualifying Microsoft engineer remote access to in-scope production systems. Production Touch Ledger, also launched with phased rollout in the EU and EFTA, creates tamper-evident records of that access and the actions performed.Azure Key Vault Managed Hardware Security Module (HSM) already gives customers dedicated, single-tenant protection and control over the encryption keys used by supported Azure services. Last year, we committed to extending that control beyond Microsoft infrastructure. External key management with Azure Managed HSM is now generally available, allowing customers to keep the root encryption key in hardware they own and operate on-premises or through a trusted third party. This gives organizations another option for workloads that require physical control of key hardware outside Microsoft infrastructure.Azure confidential computing helps protect supported data while it is processed in a hardware-based and attested trusted execution environment. We are also increasing transparency into the technologies that underpin that trust. Azure Confidential Clean Rooms, now in limited preview, applies confidential computing to approved multiparty collaboration, allowing participants to analyze shared sensitive data while limiting broader exposure of the underlying information.Together, these capabilities provide additional technical and operational controls that can support a broader digital sovereignty strategy aligned to an organization’s legal, policy, security, resilience and business requirements.Designing for resilience and operational independenceFor some workloads, digital sovereignty also means maintaining critical operations as connectivity, geopolitical and operating conditions change. Resilience must be designed from the start so essential workloads can continue operating through disruption.To help customers prepare for these scenarios, we are publishing new sovereign business continuity guidance and architecture patterns. These resources help organizations translate resilience requirements into architectures they can plan, implement and test before they are needed.For many workloads, the scale and geographic reach of the public cloud provide a strong foundation for resilience across locations and operating conditions. For workloads that require greater operational independence, Sovereign Private Cloud extends that continuum into customer-operated environments. It supports connected and disconnected operating models. The ability to transition workloads from connected to disconnected operations is entering public preview, giving organizations greater flexibility to sustain critical services as connectivity and operating requirements change.Bringing more of the application lifecycle under local controlOperational independence requires more than infrastructure. Increasingly, organizations need data, development tools, model capabilities and productivity services their applications depend on to operate within the same customer-controlled environment.Sovereign Private Cloud, built on Azure Local, extends Microsoft cloud capabilities into environments that customers operate and control. SQL Server on Azure Local is already generally available for connected and disconnected deployments. DocumentDB and Blob Storage on Azure Local are both entering public preview, giving organizations more choice in how they run and manage critical data within customer-controlled environments.GitHub Enterprise Local will become generally available at Microsoft Ignite as a validated GitHub Enterprise Server appliance on Azure Local, helping organizations keep repositories, code and development artifacts under local control. Developers can also use GitHub Copilot with locally hosted models for inference, bringing AI-assisted development closer to their code and data within the environments they control.The local application environment is expanding with Foundry Local. At Ignite, Foundry Local will become generally available for connected and disconnected operations on Azure Local, with an expanded model catalog that includes Microsoft, partner, open-weight and open-source models. Local inference and agentic retrieval will also enable users to interact with local enterprise data using natural language and receive responses grounded in that data. Integration with Microsoft 365 Local, available in preview for approved customers, extends this functionality to locally operated Microsoft SharePoint and Exchange servers.Confidential virtual machines on Azure Local are generally available, extending confidential computing capabilities to customer-controlled infrastructure. Hardware-encrypted memory and hardware-based isolation help protect sensitive data while it is being processed. Workload attestation adds assurance before sensitive data or keys are released. For regulated, sensitive and mission-critical workloads, these safeguards provide another layer of protection while giving organizations greater control over where their data and applications run.Azure Local will support multitenancy, allowing organizations to separate resources, governance and management across multiple tenants while sharing the underlying infrastructure. This significantly expands what customers with distinct business units or security boundaries can achieve with Sovereign Private Cloud. Multitenancy also creates new opportunities for local operators and service providers to deliver differentiated sovereign cloud services on Azure Local infrastructure.These additions bring more of the application lifecycle under local control, spanning data, development, productivity, AI and operations. Organizations can determine what runs locally based on the requirements of each workload.Extending the continuum through partnersGraphic titled "Sovereign Partner Ecosystem" with the subtitle "National clouds · Software · Services · Platform co-innovation," showing 32 partner logos: Accenture, AMD, Armada, Avanade, base-it, Bleu, Capgemini, Cirrus Data, CloudCasa by Catalogic, Cronos Groep, cTelecoms, DataON, Delos Cloud, Dell Technologies, F5, Felo, Fortinet, HPE, Inspark, Intel, Lenovo, Mattermost, Mistral, NVIDIA, Qualidev, Qumulo, RiverMeadow, Rubrik, Supermicro, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Veeam and WSO2.Navigating sovereignty is increasingly complex. Regulatory, security, operational and business requirements vary across countries, industries and workloads. Organizations must translate these needs into technology and operating models that work in their local context. Meeting these needs often requires a combination of technology, local operating authority, sector expertise and specialized solutions.The Sovereign Partner Ecosystem broadens the ways customers can address these requirements. National Partner Clouds, including Bleu Cloud in France and Delos Cloud in Germany, provide independently operated environments for customers that require a different ownership and operating model. Software partners can enhance Azure Local environments with capabilities across security, identity, observability, backup and recovery, migration, data, networking and applications. Digital sovereignty specialized partners combine Microsoft technologies with local knowledge and implementation expertise. Platform co-innovation partners expand infrastructure choice from datacenter to the edge.This ecosystem gives customers the flexibility to combine technology, operating models and trusted expertise based on the requirements of each workload.The next chapter of digital sovereigntyAI is amplifying both the opportunity and the impact of technology choices. As AI systems and agents interact with sensitive data, business processes and essential infrastructure, they also expand the security considerations organizations need to manage. Organizations need clear control over where these systems run, who can operate them, what actions they can take and how critical services continue when conditions change.Microsoft Sovereign Cloud brings these choices together as a continuum of control across the public cloud, customer-operated environments and our partner ecosystem. It gives organizations the flexibility to apply the appropriate level of control to each workload while continuing to benefit from cloud capabilities and ongoing innovation.We will continue to expand this continuum so organizations can innovate with cloud and AI while maintaining the control, confidentiality, resilience and operational authority their most important workloads require."
Article Summary: Microsoft has announced new cloud and AI tools aimed at giving businesses and governments greater control over their data, systems and digital operations. The updates were announced on October 20 via a blog post written by Douglas Phillips – President and Chief Technology Officer, Microsoft Specialized Clouds. The changes include new tools to monitor data access, manage encryption keys and run AI models locally.

Article Title: Michael Dell built one of the world’s biggest computer companies; his daughter Kira chose water sustainability and became CEO of an Austin startup
Article Text:
Kira Dell ’s career in water sustainability leads to CEO role at Adaptive Water

Kira Dell takes a different career path from Michael Dell

Kira’s work in Texas extends beyond her company

Dell siblings pursue separate business ventures

How Michael and Susan Dell raised their four children

Michael Dell built his fortune by turning a personal computer business into one of the world’s largest technology companies. His daughter Kira has chosen a different industry, taking on a problem that has little to do with selling computers. Based in Austin, Texas, she became chief executive of Adaptive Water in 2025, a company focused on improving the sustainability of the state’s water supply. Her career began in teaching before moving into product management, eventually leading her into the water sector. While her father’s business grew around computer hardware and enterprise technology, Kira has concentrated on a resource that communities, industries and households depend on every day.Kira Dell’s route to the executive role began outside the technology industry. She graduated from Vassar College in 2015 with a degree in international studies, according to her LinkedIn profile. Her education also included study at the School for International Training and the University of Alaska Fairbanks.She initially worked as a teacher before moving into product management, a role that brought her into the development and organisation of products and services.That experience preceded her move into the water sector. In 2025, she became chief executive of Adaptive Water, an Austin-based company working to advance water sustainability in Texas.Adaptive Water’s stated aim is to help accelerate the state’s transition towards more sustainable water use. Kira’s role puts her at the head of a business addressing that challenge, rather than in the technology sector where her father built his career. The available biographical information does not suggest that she followed a conventional route through Dell Technologies before taking the position.Michael Dell founded the company that became Dell Technologies in 1984, initially building computers around a direct-sales model. The business expanded over the following decades, becoming a major supplier of personal computers, servers and other technology used by individuals and organisations. Its growth established Michael as one of the wealthiest figures in the industry.Kira’s work at Adaptive Water represents a clear difference in professional focus. Rather than developing hardware or technology infrastructure, she leads a company concerned with the management of a natural resource. Water sustainability involves its own commercial and operational demands, including finding practical ways to address supply pressures and support more efficient use.Alongside her position at Adaptive Water, Kira serves on the board of Texas Water Trade, an organisation involved in water-related issues in the state. The role connects her corporate work with a broader network concerned with water management and sustainability.Her career has moved through education and product management into executive leadership, with water becoming its central focus. Public information about her professional background is more limited than the record of her father’s career, but her appointment as chief executive in 2025 marked a significant step in her own business life.The Dell family remains closely associated with technology through Michael’s company and his public profile. Kira’s work, however, is centred on a different challenge facing Texas. At Adaptive Water, she is leading a business seeking to make the state’s water use more sustainable, in a field where the demands of households, businesses and communities must be considered together.Her brother Zach has also pursued an entrepreneurial career in Austin, although in a separate area. He graduated from the University of Southern California in 2019, studying social sciences, psychology and economics, before beginning his career in private equity. In 2023, he co-founded Base Power Company, which provides residential battery systems designed to supply electricity during outages and support the wider grid during periods of high demand.Michael and Susan Dell married in 1989 and raised four children together: Alexa, Kira, Juliette and Zach. The family made its home in Austin, where the Dells lived on a large estate known as The Castle. Michael’s work at Dell Technologies placed him among the most prominent figures in the technology industry, but his children were not expected to follow an identical route simply because of the family name.In an October 2025 interview with Timeless Partners, Michael described how the household operated despite the financial comfort his success provided. He said the children were expected to earn or save for the things they wanted rather than assume their parents would provide them. The approach, he explained, involved maintaining rules and expectations at home, even when the family had the means to make life easier.
Article Summary: Kira Dell became chief executive of Adaptive Water in 2025. The company is focused on improving the sustainability of the state's water supply. Her career began in teaching before moving into product management. Her brother Zach has also pursued an entrepreneurial career in Austin.

Article Title: AI-generated analysis may slow strategic decisions without human oversight
Article Text: Companies risk making slower and poorer strategic decisions despite using artificial intelligence (AI) to speed up analysis, as executives struggle to review the growing volume of AI-generated output and verify its underlying assumptions, according to a report by McKinsey.The report said AI has accelerated research, data analysis and scenario planning, but human judgment remains essential for interpreting findings, assessing risks and taking responsibility for major decisions."Analysis now runs on AI time, but judgment still runs on human time," the report said, identifying the gap between the speed of AI tools and the time leaders need to make informed decisions as a growing challenge for businesses.McKinsey cited an example of a strategy team that reduced five weeks of financial analysis to less than two days using AI. However, faster output does not necessarily translate into quicker decisions, as executives may need additional time to understand the assumptions and data behind the findings.The report further identified three risks for companies: prioritising efficiency over the quality of decisions, overwhelming senior leaders with a growing volume of analysis, and reducing opportunities for junior employees to develop the judgment needed for future leadership roles.It warned that employees build decision-making skills through practical experience, feedback and repeated problem-solving. If AI takes over these tasks without alternative training, companies could weaken their pipeline of future strategy leaders.To address these risks, McKinsey recommended that companies reserve senior executives' attention for decisions involving greater uncertainty and higher stakes, while allowing AI to support or automate routine decisions within clearly defined limits.It also called for structured training to help employees understand and verify AI-generated analysis, including the assumptions and calculations behind it. Companies should assign clear responsibility to individuals for consequential decisions, even when AI tools contribute to the analysis."The winners will not be the organisations that automate the most decisions. They will be the ones that make the best use of AI's speed while protecting the human judgment that AI cannot replace," the report said.McKinsey added that faster analysis could allow businesses to review resource allocation more frequently, including moving from annual reviews to quarterly or monthly assessments.
Article Summary: Companies risk making slower and poorer strategic decisions despite using artificial intelligence (AI) to speed up analysis. Executives struggle to review the growing volume of AI-generated output and verify its underlying assumptions, according to a report by McKinsey. AI has accelerated research, data analysis and scenario planning, but human judgment remains essential.

Article Title: Xbox CEO is reportedly planning three more rounds of job cuts; starting this month, layoffs are part of what CEO Asha Sharma described as 'fundamental reset of how Xbox operates and invests'
Article Text:
'Fundamental reset' of Xbox operations

Xbox job cuts: Employees demoralised

Studios and strategy under review

Why Xbox is being reset

Questions about Xbox’s future

Microsoft’s Xbox division is reportedly preparing for three additional rounds of layoffs over the coming months as CEO Asha Sharma pushed ahead with a sweeping restructuring aimed at improving the gaming business’ financial performance. According to a report by Fortune, Sharma is planning some more job cuts this month, followed by some additional rounds in November and January, extending a shake-up that has already resulted in thousands of layoffs across Microsoft’s gaming operations. In July this year, Asha Sharman announced plans to eliminate approximately 3,200 jobs during Microsoft's fiscal 2027, including around 1,600 positions that were cut immediately. A further round of layoffs affecting roughly 260 employees followed in September. Microsoft has not publicly confirmed the latest reported plans or disclosed how many employees could be affected.The layoffs are part of what Asha Sharma has previously described as a fundamental reset of how Xbox operates and invests. In a message to employees earlier this year, she said the business was not healthy and acknowledged that Xbox was operating with margins significantly below those of comparable platform and publishing companies.Sharma argued that years of heavy investment in content, hardware, platforms and studio acquisitions had failed to deliver the level of growth Microsoft expected. The restructuring is aimed at simplifying the organisation, reducing costs and focusing resources on projects with stronger commercial prospects.Spreading the cuts over several waves has left some employees demoralised, Fortune reports. Some staff feel they are working under a yearlong cloud, waiting to see whether their roles will be next. Fortune also found at least one employee who was laid off and then offered a chance to stay. Some employees appreciated Sharma’s transparency, the report says. Sharma acknowledged the tough decisions but said she values people and does not intend to be transactional.The reset has already resulted in major changes across Microsoft's gaming portfolio. Studios including Double Fine Productions and Compulsion Games have been allowed to regain independence, while other teams have undergone reviews, reorganisations or ownership discussions as Xbox streamlines its operations.The restructuring reflects growing pressure on Microsoft's gaming division to improve profitability amid rising industry costs and a challenging console market. While speculation has emerged over Xbox's long-term future within Microsoft, Sharma recently told media outlets that Xbox is not for sale, while Microsoft executives have publicly backed her leadership of the gaming business.Sharma, 38, took over in February from longtime Xbox head Phil Spencer. She had no video game industry experience, having previously led product work on Microsoft’s AI Foundry platform. Fortune describes Xbox as a roughly $21 billion business with profit margins of about 3 percent, a fraction of what rivals earn and far below what Microsoft expects of its major units. Current Xbox consoles have sold only a little over a third as many units as the PlayStation 5, according to third-party estimates, and memory chip shortages are pushing up hardware costs. Sharma told Fortune in July that Xbox had grown by making many bets and lost focus on its core business, saying the company “spread ourselves too thin.”Several current and former staff members told Fortune they believe Xbox is being prepared for a possible sale, spinoff or other restructuring, amid heavy Microsoft spending on artificial intelligence. Judson Althoff, one of Microsoft’s most senior executives, rejected that idea, saying Microsoft would not have put Sharma in charge of a business it intends to sell. The next test comes with Microsoft’s quarterly earnings report this month, and Sharma has said she expects financial improvements to show in Microsoft’s fiscal 2027.
Article Summary: Microsoft's Xbox division is reportedly preparing for three additional rounds of layoffs over the coming months. CEO Asha Sharma is pushing ahead with a sweeping restructuring aimed at improving the gaming business’ financial performance. In July this year, Asha Sharman announced plans to eliminate approximately 3,200 jobs during Microsoft's fiscal 2027.

Article Title: Google rolls out new Gemini tools to help small businesses save time
Article Text:
Brand-consistent visuals

Financial insights from messy records

Business owners in India and elsewhere

Availability

Google has announced a set of new Gemini tools aimed at small business owners, led by a dedicated business landing page inside the Gemini app. The company says tens of millions of small business owners already use Gemini to brainstorm products, handle customer feedback and analyse performance, and that the new tools are meant to give them time back so they can focus on the work they started their companies for. The announcement was published on Google’s India blog by Vishnu Sivaji, Senior Director of the Gemini app.The landing page is designed as a central hub where owners can build their brand, analyse finances and understand customer insights. Gemini can also now connect to Google Business Profile, Google Ads and Google Workspace, as well as third-party apps including Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho and Xero.Businesses can now define their brand style in Gemini by uploading a website, brand kit, fonts or colour palettes. Paired with Nano Banana 2.1, Google’s latest image-generation model, Gemini can produce end-to-end visuals for product launches and marketing campaigns. Google says Gemini remembers the brand style, so owners do not have to upload their guidelines each time they want new on-brand material.Gemini can also turn disorganised spreadsheets, receipts and purchase records into clear financial graphics and interactive models within seconds, according to Google.The aim is to let owners get insights in plain language rather than working through the numbers themselves.Google highlighted several users to illustrate the tools. In Maharashtra, farmer and content creator Santosh Jadhav turned his traditional fields into a ginger farm with no formal training or local mentors. He used Gemini as a virtual agronomist to judge soil suitability, calculate seed requirements and draft an investment budget, and he shares his farming journey online to show how easily AI can be used in everyday agriculture.In Jakarta, Gumilang turned a neglected space under train tracks into Barelz Arena, a sports and entertainment hub. With no background in branding or sports, he used Gemini to develop a “Brazilian-street” visual identity, design merchandise and draft partnership proposals. In Bordeaux, France, ceramicist Morgane says Gemini saves her two to three hours a day by drafting product descriptions, newsletters and social media hooks. In Goiânia, Brazil, personal organiser Patricia Morais uses Gemini for customer service and content while working on accessible products such as clothing QR codes for people with visual impairments.The business landing page, the new marketing and finance skills and the additional connected apps will begin rolling out in the coming days to all Gemini app users worldwide, Google said. For larger organisations that want centralised admin controls, data governance and enterprise-grade security, the company pointed to its separate Gemini for business offering.
Article Summary: Gemini now has a dedicated business landing page for small business owners. Businesses can define their brand style in Gemini by uploading a website, brand kit, fonts or colour palettes. Google says Gemini remembers the brand style, so owners do not have to upload their guidelines each time they want new on-brand material.
